issues.legal_issue: A person may maintain a constitutional petition when a genuine lease creates a present property right, even if the nature or extent of that right is disputed.
material_facts: A registered lease in favour of the petitioner was not alleged to be fictitious and purported to confer rights in the land immediately.
The parties disputed the nature of the rights created by the lease and whether the petitioner qualified for particular tenure statuses.
The petitioner sought relief in a petition to enforce fundamental rights.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner had standing to maintain the petition while the lease remained in force, although the Court did not decide the nature of the rights the lease conferred.
issues.legal_principle: A genuine instrument that creates a right in presenti is sufficient to support standing to seek constitutional relief, even where the precise nature of the right is disputed. The Court distinguished standing from the merits of the claimed tenure status, which involved disputed facts suitable for determination in a proper forum.

predicates.constitutional_petition: The person sought relief in a constitutional petition to enforce a fundamental right.
predicates.genuine_lease: The person relied on a lease that was not alleged to be fictitious.
predicates.lease_creates_present_right: The lease purported to create a right in the property immediately rather than only a future right.

issues.definition: When a person brings a constitutional petition relying on a genuine lease that creates a present right, that person has standing even if the right's nature remains disputed.

issues.legal_issue: A post-constitutional law that deprives a person of property without the compensation required when the law was enacted is invalid and cannot be revived by a later constitutional amendment removing the restriction.
material_facts: The challenged transfer law was enacted after the Constitution came into force and declared specified transfers void, depriving transferees of rights they would otherwise acquire.
The law did not provide for compensation for that deprivation.
A later constitutional amendment changed the constitutional rule governing compulsory acquisition, but was not retrospective.
issues.conclusion: The transfer law was unconstitutional and of no force or effect; the later constitutional amendment did not revive it.
issues.legal_principle: The constitutionality of a law is judged by the Constitution as it stood when the law was enacted, subject to a retrospective constitutional amendment. Under Articles 13(2) and 31(2), as they stood at enactment, the law contravened the constitutional protection against uncompensated deprivation of property. The Fourth Amendment was not retrospective and could not validate the law through the doctrine of eclipse, which applies to pre-constitutional laws under Article 13(1), not post-constitutional laws under Article 13(2). The Court relied on State of West Bengal v. Sabodh Gopal Bose, Saghir Ahmad v. State of U.P., Karam Singh v. Nihal Khan, Bombay Dyeing and Manufacturing Co. Ltd. v. State of Bombay, Behram Khurshed Pesikaka v. State of Bombay, Keshavan Madhava Menon v. State of Bombay, Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of Madhya Pradesh, and Deep Chand v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

predicates.constitutional_challenge: A person challenged the validity of a law in a constitutional proceeding.
predicates.post_constitution_law: The challenged law was enacted after the Constitution came into force.
predicates.deprives_property_without_required_compe: The law deprived a person of property without providing the compensation required by the constitutional rule in force when the law was enacted.
predicates.later_amendment_removes_constitutional_b: A later constitutional amendment removed the constitutional restriction that the law had contravened, without retrospectively validating the law.

issues.definition: A law enacted after the Constitution that deprives a person of property without then-required compensation remains invalid when a later amendment removes the restriction, if the amendment does not retrospectively validate it.

issues.legal_issue: Interim forest-control provisions may constitutionally regulate claimed interests while reserved-forest proceedings are pending and may apply to land whose proprietary rights have vested in the State, even if a claimant asserts tenure rights in it.
material_facts: The forest-control provisions regulated or prohibited activities while claims concerning land were being considered in proceedings to constitute reserved forests.
The provisions were enacted as an interim measure to protect forests during those proceedings.
The land had belonged to an intermediary and vested in the State under land-reform legislation.
The petitioner claimed rights as a tenure-holder, including a possible status as a bhumidhar, but a bhumidhar held tenure under the State rather than proprietary title.
The later addition of provisions concerning management of forests did not alter the character of the original provisions as ancillary to reserved-forest proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The original forest-control provisions were constitutional and applied to the land, even on the assumption that the petitioner held bhumidhari rights.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read sections 38A to 38G of the Forest Act, as amended, as ancillary to Chapter II of that Act, which governs the process of constituting reserved forests and determining claims. Their interim protection of forests pending those proceedings served the public interest. Chapter II applies to forest or waste land that is State property or over which the State has proprietary rights. Under the land-reform legislation, tenure-holders, including bhumidhars, hold under the State and are not proprietors. The Court also relied on Mst. Govindi v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge and interim_forest_controls and reserved_forest_proceedings_pending and land_proprietary_rights_vested_in_state and claimant_holds_or_claims_tenure

predicates.constitutional_challenge: A person challenged the validity or application of forest-control provisions in a constitutional proceeding.
predicates.interim_forest_controls: The challenged controls restricted activities as an interim measure to protect forest land.
predicates.reserved_forest_proceedings_pending: Proceedings to determine claims and constitute the land as reserved forest were pending.
predicates.land_proprietary_rights_vested_in_state: Proprietary rights in the land had vested in the State.
predicates.claimant_holds_or_claims_tenure: The claimant held or asserted a tenure right under the State rather than proprietary ownership.

issues.definition: If interim forest controls operate while reserved-forest claims are pending over land owned by the State, they may validly apply to a person who holds or claims tenure in that land.

issues.legal_issue: A published forest notification is not withdrawn by an unpublished administrative instruction where withdrawal must be made in the same manner as the notification.
material_facts: A notification initiating the reserved-forest process was published in the official gazette.
The government later issued an unpublished administrative instruction stating that qualifying land should be treated as excluded from the notification.
That instruction was subsequently cancelled by another unpublished government order.
issues.conclusion: The notification remained in force because it had not been withdrawn or modified by a notification published in the official gazette.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4 of the Forest Act, the notification had to be published in the official gazette. Section 21 of the U.P. General Clauses Act permitted its cancellation or modification only in the like manner and subject to the like conditions; therefore, an unpublished departmental instruction did not withdraw or modify it.

predicates.constitutional_petition: A person sought a ruling about the effect of a forest notification in a constitutional petition.
predicates.forest_notification_published: The government published a notification initiating the reserved-forest process in the official gazette.
predicates.purported_withdrawal_unpublished: The government attempted to withdraw or modify the notification by an unpublished administrative instruction.

issues.definition: When a forest notification has been published and the government attempts to withdraw it only through an unpublished instruction, the notification remains in force.
